classification_rule: REJECT requires check rc!=0, build --strict --sanitize=none rc!=0, and a [CPLUS- tagged diagnostic; both rc==0 is ACCEPT; rejection without [CPLUS- is GAP-UNTAGGED.

expected_for_all_cases.diagnostic_family: use-after-free / use-after-move at the use site
expected_for_all_cases.note: Expectations only. Observed classifications are recorded per case and are intentionally not overwritten.

cases.gap: false negative: guarded drop never reaches the post-if use
cases.cfg_fact: At the if join, s is Live on the false edge and Released on the true edge: join = MaybeReleased. A use (s.at(0)) in MaybeReleased must be rejected. Requires edge-sensitive merge at the join.

cases.scenario: conditional move: if (flag) b = cplus_move(a); ... a.size()
cases.gap: rejected without a [CPLUS- tag; path-insensitive tracker; diagnostic mis-located to the following print statement (line 25 col 29) instead of a.size() on line 24
cases.cfg_fact: At the if join, a is MovedFrom on the true edge and Live on the false edge (MaybeMovedFrom), and b is MaybeOwning. Reject a.size() on the may-move path and treat b's scope-exit drop as conditional. A use in the else branch only must NOT be rejected (probe D).

cases.scenario: mixed-path initialization: release in one branch, use after join
cases.gap: false negative: if/else states are not phi-merged
cases.cfg_fact: At the if/else join, owner s has {Released (then), Live (else)} -> MaybeReleased. The use after the join must be rejected on the released path. Merge per-predecessor states keyed by owner identity, not by source line or fallthrough only.

cases.scenario: loop-carried release: release inside a loop, use after loop
cases.gap: false negative: release inside nested if in a loop is not carried across the back-edge
cases.cfg_fact: The loop header merges entry state with the back-edge state. After i==0 the owner is Released; fixed-point iteration propagates that to the loop exit -> MaybeReleased at s.at(0). Requires back-edge modelling and iteration to a fixed point.

guarded release is invisible to the liveness checker

supplementary_probes.conclusion: loop-carried release is invisible to the liveness checker

supplementary_probes.conclusion: move tracker is path-insensitive and emits a false positive; a CFG analysis must suppress it
